scope: Pinned native API response decoder dependencies and accounting argument. Integrated into the internal standalone API candidate; public API, full transport memory and release acceptance remain separate gates.
accounting: The compressed body remains owned while decoding. Decoded output, 64 KiB scratch, working state and original/replacement output capacities hold simultaneous paired context/engine reservations.

The zlib reservation is 128 KiB: one allocation containing aligned inflate state and 32 KiB window, plus temporary initialization state and wrapper. A test checks the exact pinned state layout. No gzip header capture target is configured, so optional fields are scanned from retained input without another variable-size copy. Concatenated members drop the preceding decoder before creating the next.

Brotli reserves fixed state size and every dynamically allocated typed buffer capacity. The first allocation error is sticky across allocator clones and frees. Constructor and every decode call check this original error before consuming output.

In the pinned Brotli source an unchecked initial length-table allocation failure forces the later checked ring-buffer allocation to fail before table use. Group-index failure likewise forces the following checked code-table allocation to fail. No production panic recovery is used.
Decoder calls are bounded to 64 KiB input/output chunks and yield after 1 MiB combined progress. Cancellation or owner closure releases workspace by dropping the original future.

validationContract.limitations: Focused exact-source tests; native API transport integration and supported-platform release acceptance remain required.
